title: The Efficacy and Safety of Dalfampridine on Cognition and Fatigue in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Halabi MH, Alromayan R, Almutairi M, Alasmari H, AlGhamdi MA, Makkawi S
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system. People with MS frequently experience cognitive dysfunction and fatigue. Dalfampridine (DAL), a potassium channel blocker, is US Food and Drug Administration-approved for the treatment of walking impairment in people with MS. It may also enhance nerve conduction in regions associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate DAL's efficacy in improving these symptoms, as well as its safety profile, in people with MS. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science, covering all records from database inception through April 1, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DAL with placebo in people with MS and reporting impaired cognition and fatigue were included. A random-effects model was used to calculate the risk ratio (RR), standardized mean difference (SMD), and mean difference (MD) with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Of 1329 studies identified, 13 RCTs involving a total of 827 people with MS were included. DAL demonstrated a significant improvement in cognitive symptoms (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.38; P = .01; I² = 6%). However, no significant difference was observed between DAL and placebo in reducing fatigue (MD = 3.70; 95% CI, -4.37 to 11.77;P = .37; I² = 19%). Safety measures were comparable, with no significant difference in adverse events (RR = 1.11; 95% CI, 0.99-1.25; P = .08; I² = 0%). CONCLUSIONS: People with MS receiving DAL demonstrated significant improvement in cognitive symptoms; however, further studies are warranted to validate and confirm this finding.

title: Acute multi-organ dysfunction (aMOD): Brighton Collaboration case definition and guidelines for data collection, analysis, and presentation of immunization safety data.
authors: O'Connor C, Jacob ST, Levy JH, Nwagha T, Ramesh D, Munoz FM, Farnon EC, Law B
abstract: This is a new Brighton Collaboration case definition of acute multi-organ dysfunction (aMOD) as an adverse event following immunization (AEFI). It is intended for use in clinical trials and post-licensure pharmacovigilance activities to facilitate safety data comparability across multiple settings. It is not intended to guide clinical management, but it can serve as an outcome measure of disease severity in the context of vaccine efficacy and effectiveness studies. The case definition was developed by a group of subject matter and Brighton Collaboration process experts as part of the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI)-funded Safety Platform for Evaluation of vACcines (SPEAC). The Brighton Collaboration case definition includes a scoping review of the literature and expert consensus used to define levels of diagnostic certainty (LOC) for aMOD and provides specific guidelines for related data collection and analysis. The document underwent peer review by a Reference Group of vaccine safety stakeholders and aMOD experts to ensure case definition useability, applicability, and scientific integrity. aMOD is defined as acute dysfunction involving two or more of six organ systems: respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, neurologic, hepatic, and hemostatic. A key feature is the requirement that organ dysfunction occur within the same clinical episode, with onset within 7 days, allowing sequential or simultaneous involvement. Five LOC are included for each of the six organs. The overall aMOD case definition also comprises five LOC categories: Level 1 (Definite), Level 2 (Probable), Level 3 (Possible), Level 4 (Insufficient information), and Level 5 (Not a case). The criteria build on established organ dysfunction frameworks while adapting them for global application. Importantly, AEFI case definitions are separate from causality assessment. This case definition provides a standardized approach to aMOD case ascertainment, bridging concepts of organ dysfunction with Brighton Collaboration requirements for reproducible vaccine safety assessment. It also provides a standard case definition that can be used by stakeholders to harmonize assessment of AEFI to enable rigorous analysis and comparison of AEFI surveillance across settings and studies.

title: Liver fibrosis risk, missed follow-up, and inequitable specialist referral in the All of Us Research Program: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Sellers K, White TM, Manolas MI, Hagström H, Brennan PN, Diaz LA, Bansal MB, Danpanichkul P
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent and frequently undiagnosed, despite liver fibrosis being the strongest predictor of liver-related morbidity and mortality. We aimed to quantify Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index-based fibrosis risk and to evaluate guideline-recommended follow-up-FIB-4 documentation, confirmatory testing, and specialist referral-in a large US cohort. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of electronic health record data from the US All of Us Research Program. Among adults aged 35 years or older with sufficient laboratory data, FIB-4 scores were calculated from routinely captured biomarkers, classified as low (<1.3), indeterminate (1.3-2.67; 2.0-2.67 if aged ≥65 years), or high risk (>2.67), and described across sociodemographic and metabolic subgroups; associations with incident major adverse liver outcomes (MALO) were assessed with Cox proportional-hazards regression. We examined FIB-4 documentation, confirmatory testing, and specialty referrals within 365 days of the index FIB-4 date. FINDINGS: Among 136,004 participants (mean age 60.8 years [SD 13.5]; 79,365 [58.4%] female; 81,420 [59.9%] White, 21,779 [16.0%] Hispanic or Latino, 20,076 [14.8%] Black), 26,971 (19.8%, 95% CI 19.6-20.0) had indeterminate and 11,217 (8.2%, 8.1-8.4) high FIB-4-based fibrosis risk. Elevated risk was more frequent with cardiovascular disease (41.7% vs 25.6%), hypertension (30.7% vs 23.4%), and type 2 diabetes (29.7% vs 27.4%), rising from 25.6% with no metabolic comorbidities to 36.6% with four. FIB-4 documentation was rare, and fewer than 1% of high-risk participants underwent confirmatory testing or referral; referral was low across risk categories (0.19% high, 0.19% indeterminate, 0.25% low risk). MALO occurred in 1308 (11.7%) high-risk vs 830 (0.8%) low-risk participants (adjusted hazard ratio 19.68, 95% CI 17.88-21.67). INTERPRETATION: Routinely collected laboratory data identify substantial liver fibrosis risk in this volunteer US cohort, yet guideline-recommended follow-up is uncommon. Implementation strategies such as automated risk calculation and reflex-based testing pathways could reduce missed opportunities for earlier diagnosis and intervention. FUNDING: No specific funding was received for this study.

title: A topologically engineered hydrogel platform targeting IL11 promotes renal repair after partial nephrectomy.
authors: Yu Z, Dong X, Li F, Zhang Y, Dai S, Cao N, Jia X, Zhao J
abstract: Partial nephrectomy (PN) is the gold standard for treating renal tumors and trauma; however, massive nephron loss and persistent fibrosis readily lead to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Current therapeutic options remain non-curative and costly, as nearly half of PN patients inevitably progress to end-stage renal failure. Here, we present an innovative regenerative platform for PN-induced CKD, integrating structural biomimicry with targeted molecular inhibition. Harnessing light-based bioprinting of gelatin and hyaluronic acid methacrylates coupled with removable alginate microfiber, we constructed a hierarchical channel scaffold (HCS) that features precisely patterned macrochannels and template-derived microchannels, which closely mimics native kidney architecture, provides structural support, and remarkably enhances cell migration (∼5.45-fold) and rapid neovascularization (∼7.66-fold) over unidirectional channel structures. Moreover, interleukin 11 (IL11) was identified as a novel therapeutic target in kidney fibrosis after PN. Thus, extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells loaded with IL11 small interfering RNA (siIL11) were homogeneously encapsulated into HCS, achieving over 4-fold higher renal retention than systemic delivery in PN-induced CKD mice. Furthermore, sustained local release of EV-siIL11 and hierarchically channeled HCS guided synergistic regenerative effects that remarkably inhibited fibrosis, cell cycle arrest, and immune responses, thereby potently preventing kidney atrophy and restoring renal structure with newly aligned nephrons and vasculature, ultimately recovering kidney function. Further analysis revealed that IL11 silencing reversed epithelial‒mesenchymal transition by suppressing the STAT3-ERK-GSK3β-SNAI1 axis. This topological multifunctional hydrogel platform offers a localized, sustained, and clinically translatable strategy for postsurgical kidney regeneration.

title: MR Clinics-Nuclear Medicine in Renal, Adrenal, Bladder and Urothelial Malignancies.
authors: Romsa J, Sutherland D, Akincioglu C
journal: Magnetic resonance imaging clinics of North America
abstract: Nuclear medicine is a rapidly evolving specialty with investment and innovation currently outpacing much of medicine. Advancements in instrumentation in PET and single-photon emission computed tomography imaging coupled with advances in targeted radionuclide therapy have positioned nuclear medicine as a critical pillar of oncology. In this article, we explore applications in renal, adrenal, bladder, and urothelial malignancies.

title: Engineering copper homeostasis for microenvironment-adaptive therapy in inflammation-driven disorders.
authors: Ding F, Liu J, Liu M, Huang H, Tang H, Zhong J, Liu C, Liu Z
abstract: Inflammation-driven disorders (IDDs) arise from distinct initiating events, yet many persist because immune activation, oxidative and metabolic stress, regulated cell death, and tissue remodeling form self-reinforcing local niches. Copper connects these processes through its roles as a cuproenzyme cofactor, redox-active species and dynamically trafficked regulatory metal. Its therapeutic significance, however, is determined by disease stage, cell type, subcellular distribution and chemical state. Copper deficiency, excess or mislocalization may therefore be adaptive, protective or pathogenic in different contexts. This review develops a disease- and copper-state-specific framework that links copper homeostasis to therapeutic platform design. We first examine inflammation-associated remodeling of copper trafficking and compare representative copper states in autoimmune joint disease, metabolic inflammation, fibrosis, inflammation-associated cancer and infection-associated tissue repair. We then critically evaluate copper-dependent and copper-sensitive mechanisms governing inflammatory mediator availability, immune-cell programming and checkpoint regulation, regulated cell death, angiogenesis and stromal remodeling, while distinguishing direct mechanistic evidence from model-dependent inference. Building on this analysis, we compare pharmacological modulators with nanocarriers, copper-containing active materials and local copper-sequestering platforms that implement copper chelation or sequestration, controlled copper delivery or release, intracellular redistribution, and catalytic activation or nanozyme-like redox regulation. We further outline how pathological copper pools, activation cues, release kinetics, speciation, biodistribution and target engagement should be measured so that precision is demonstrated rather than inferred from material composition. This framework positions copper modulation as a context-specific complement to existing therapy and defines the mechanistic, analytical and translational evidence required for microenvironment-adaptive treatment of IDDs.

title: Spatial mechanopriming of multicellular interfaces drives cytoskeletal-to-nuclear remodeling to boost therapeutic efficacy of stem cells.
authors: Bayaraa O, Lee NH, Kim SH, Lee H, Li CJ, Fu X, Hyun J, Choi G
abstract: Engineering multicellular constructs through biophysical cues, independent of soluble biochemical factors, is a promising strategy to boost the therapeutic potential of stem cells for regenerative medicine. However, the mechanisms by which spatially organized cell-cell and cell-matrix interfaces govern multicellular signaling and subsequent behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate these mechanistic events by introducing 2D nanoplates (∼350 nm) compartmentalized within the intercellular space of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroids to form de novo cell-matrix spatial interfaces. These interfaces redistribute internal stress across the spheroid, amplifying integrin-cytoskeleton-nucleus force transmission and restoring YAP-dependent mechanotransduction to achieve spatial mechanopriming. Cells within these mechanoprimed spheroids exhibit profound nuclear deformation, epigenetic remodeling, and spatially patterned metabolic activation. Finite element modeling and spatial transcriptomic analyses further reveal a spheroid-wide reorganization of cytoskeletal and transcriptional networks. Mechanistically, elevated cytoskeletal tension across the reorganized interfaces is associated with a putative, tension-associated pseudo-hypoxic signature involving HIF-1α-related signaling, establishing a mechanometabolic niche that robustly enhances angiogenic secretion. Consequently, mechanoprimed spheroids demonstrate superior engraftment, accelerated vascular regeneration, and improved perfusion recovery in a murine ischemia model. Collectively, this work establishes spatial mechanopriming as an effective strategy to remodel cytoskeletal-to-nuclear mechanics and enhance the therapeutic potential of 3D multicellular systems.

title: A let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicle-laden bioactive scaffold promotes immunomodulation and regeneration of segmental tracheal defects.
authors: Liu B, Wei N, Liang L, Shi Z, Liu P, Zeng T, Zhang H, Zhang H
abstract: Segmental tracheal defects resulting from trauma, tumor resection, or congenital malformations pose significant challenges for reconstruction. Persistent post-injury inflammation, inadequate neovascularization, and delayed epithelial restoration contribute to the formation of granulation tissue and subsequent graft failure. In this study, we developed a bioactive tracheal scaffold for sustained local delivery of let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicles (let-7a-5p-EVs) to modulate the regenerative microenvironment during tracheal repair. The scaffold was constructed by integrating a mechanically optimized polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a 20% Pluronic F127 hydrogel, which served as a local reservoir for EV retention and sustained release. Let-7a-5p-EVs were generated from lentivirally engineered human gingiva-derived mesenchymal stem cells and showed typical EV morphology, representative EV marker expression, and efficient uptake by airway epithelial cells. In vitro, let-7a-5p-EVs enhanced airway epithelial cell migration and shifted lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophages from a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype toward a reparative M2-like phenotype, accompanied by reduced inflammatory cytokine expression. In a rabbit segmental tracheal defect model, the let-7a-5p-EV-laden scaffold enhanced neovascularization, mitigated local inflammatory responses, promoted mucociliary epithelial reconstruction, and maintained airway patency. The let-7a-5p-EV scaffold improved biomechanical recovery, and increased survival rates. Transcriptomic profiling and molecular validation indicated that these effects were associated with the attenuation of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)-associated inflammatory activation, as evidenced by reduced p65 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. These findings demonstrate that sustained local delivery of engineered EVs from a mechanically competent bioactive scaffold provides an effective immunomodulatory strategy for the regenerative repair of segmental tracheal defects and offers translational potential for functional airway reconstruction.

title: LILRB3 as an ulcerative colitis-associated molecular biomarker: integrated transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental validation.
authors: Yang B, Sun D, Liu Z, Zhou L
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by mucosal inflammation and immune dysregulation. Although macrophage-mediated inflammation is associated with UC progression, its molecular basis remains incompletely understood. This study integrated bioinformatic analyses and experimental validation to identify UC-associated molecular biomarkers and explore their roles in immune dysregulation. METHODS: Bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated for differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and multi-algorithm machine learning. The machine-learning model was evaluated in independent validation cohorts, and a nomogram was subsequently constructed and evaluated in an additional colonic-tissue cohort. Immune infiltration, single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication, pseudotime analysis, and scTenifoldKnk-based virtual knockout were used to investigate hub genes. RT-qPCR, WB, and IHC validated the findings in a DSS-induced mouse model and clinical samples, while siRNA-mediated LILRB3 knockdown was performed in THP-1-derived macrophages. RESULTS: Differential expression analysis and WGCNA identified 55 candidate genes. Through screening of 127 machine-learning algorithm combinations, DPP10, LILRB3, MTMR11, and SLC6A14 were identified as UC-associated molecular biomarkers. A separately constructed logistic regression nomogram showed an apparent AUC of 0.989. LILRB3 was predominantly expressed in myeloid cells, particularly M1 macrophages, and was associated with inflammatory immune cell infiltration. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed that LILRB3⁺ M1 macrophages exhibited active intercellular communication involving MHC-II-CD4 and other inflammation-related signaling pathways. Experimental validation showed increased PirB expression in the colonic tissues of DSS-induced colitis mice and elevated LILRB3 expression in human UC colonic tissues. Knockdown of LILRB3 in THP-1-derived macrophages significantly reduced TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β mRNA expression. CONCLUSION: LILRB3 is a candidate UC-associated molecular biomarker in colonic tissue and may be associated with proinflammatory macrophage remodeling and myeloid immune dysregulation, warranting mechanistic investigation.

title: Development of a novel near-infrared fluorescent probe for nitroxyl imaging in acute kidney injury.
authors: Wang Z, Wang C, Zhang R, Xiao N, Yu T, Shi C, Xiang X, Shu W
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Nitroxyl (HNO), a short-lived reactive nitrogen species, participates in regulating cellular redox and nitrosative homeostasis, and its level fluctuations may reflect biochemical alterations associated with renal tubular injury during acute kidney injury (AKI). Therefore, the development of HNO fluorescent probes for AKI models may help visualize HNO-related changes under kidney injury conditions. In this study, we developed a near-infrared fluorescent probe DCM-HNO based on a dicyanoisophorone fluorophore and a 2-(diphenylphosphino)benzoate HNO-responsive unit. Upon triggering of the phosphine-mediated uncaging process by HNO, the fluorophore is released and the intramolecular charge transfer is restored, resulting in enhanced fluorescence at 700 nm. DCM-HNO exhibited a large Stokes shift of 155 nm, a low detection limit of 76 nM, and good resistance to interference. The low-cytotoxic probe enabled imaging of exogenous HNO and chemically generated intracellular HNO in HK-2 cells. In cisplatin-injured HK-2 cells, the fluorescence signal increased with rising cisplatin concentration and decreased upon N-acetylcysteine treatment, confirming the capability of DCM-HNO to visualize HNO-related fluorescence changes during cellular AKI. Ex vivo kidney imaging further showed enhanced fluorescence in kidneys from cisplatin-induced AKI mice. Moreover, significantly stronger fluorescence was exhibited by ischemia-reperfusion kidneys compared with untreated contralateral kidneys. Collectively, DCM-HNO may be considered a near-infrared imaging tool for monitoring HNO-associated alterations in cellular and mouse models of AKI.

title: A biosynthetic paradox implicating dynamic zeaxanthin biosynthesis at the ER-LD interface.
authors: Sun L, Zhang J, Abdullah CN, Shen Y, Geng S, Xu S, Zhou J
abstract: Traditional metabolic engineering often treats lipid droplets (LDs) as inert storage sinks and assumes shortening enzyme-substrate distance inherently enhances pathway efficiency. Harnessing Yarrowia lipolytica for zeaxanthin production, we uncovered a pivotal "spatial paradox" challenging this conventional dogma. A selective shielding strategy first identified the hydroxylase PaCrtZ as the primary biosynthetic bottleneck. Subcellular localization trials revealed that directly targeting PaCrtZ to the β-carotene-rich LD surface unexpectedly yielded the lowest zeaxanthin relative fraction (9.87%), significantly underperforming compared to cytosolic (27.15%) or peroxisomal targeting (43.16%). To investigate this counterintuitive phenomenon, multidimensional engineering strategies were implemented to boost zeaxanthin accumulation. Subsequently, in situ, label-free stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy unequivocally demonstrated the co-localization of β-carotene and zeaxanthin within LDs, confirming that substrate inaccessibility was not the limiting factor. Guided by principles of LD biogenesis, these findings led us to conceptualize a dynamic endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-LD interface functional microenvironment model. We propose that robust PaCrtZ-catalyzed hydroxylation is sustained predominantly at transient ER-LD junctions, where hydrophobic β-carotene "skimming" is dynamically synchronized with efficient O2 and NADPH cofactor exchange. This model redefines lipid organelles as active, organized metabolic hubs beyond mere storage, offering a novel transformative framework for future organelle-targeted metabolic interface design.

title: Dopamine depletion induces low frequency beta oscillations through a minimal loop in basal ganglia: A computational study.
authors: Su X, Shi X, Bai B
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: Pathological β-band oscillations in the cortex and basal ganglia (BG) are a core electrophysiological hallmark of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet the precise circuits and temporal dynamics governing their emergence remain incompletely understood. To address this, we developed a computational model of the chronically dopamine-depleted BG and identified a minimal inhibitory microcircuit as a primary generator of network wide β oscillations, which is composed of D2-medium spiny neurons (D2-MSN), fast spiking interneurons (FSI), and prototypic external globus pallidus neurons (GPe-TI). By simulating progressive dopamine loss, we show that distinct synaptic pathways within this loop are engaged in a stage-dependent manner: FSI → D2-MSN projection dominates during early to mid depletion stages, whereas GPe-TI → FSI inhibition prevails in later phases. This temporal shift is accompanied by a progressive slowing of the peak oscillation frequency from 11-13 Hz oscillation to 9-11 Hz oscillation. Overall, our results provide a dynamic, circuit level account for how pathological β rhythms evolve over the course of dopamine depletion, offering a mechanistic framework for understanding stage specific pathophysiology in PD and a novel paradigm for designing adaptive neuromodulation strategies.

title: Genetically engineered extracellular vesicles with chimeric antigen receptors of human stem cell-derived neutrophils targeting fibroblast activation protein to modulate tumor microenvironment.
authors: Esmonde C, Sun L, Jin G, Michaelides L, Syed F, Bhattarai J, Driscoll T, Quiñones-Hinojosa A
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most commonly occurring central nervous system tumor, accounting for over 50% of gliomas, with a poor survival rate. A primary driver of GBM progression is the fibrotic stroma, where excess extracellular matrix deposition creates a dense network that excludes immune cells and chemotherapeutic agents. While targeting tumor-associated fibroblasts (TAFs) via fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cells is a promising strategy, off-target toxicities limit the clinical utility of the treatment. To address these safety concerns, extracellular vesicles (EVs) of FAP-CAR-engineered neutrophils differentiated from human pluripotent stem cells were isolated and characterized, including proteomic profile, microRNA content, in vitro bioactivity, and in vivo biodistribution in this study. Multi-omic profiling revealed that CAR engineering enriched EVs with proinflammatory proteins, iron-transferring proteins, and proliferation regulators, and a significant upregulation of miRNAs targeting FAP and proliferation-regulating genes was observed. Functional in vitro assays demonstrated that these EVs are selectively cytotoxic to TAFs, reducing the expression of BCL-2 and RAS-MAPK-ERK signaling pathway genes. These EVs also demonstrated cytotoxicity to patient-derived GBM spheroids. Furthermore, in vivo biodistribution results confirmed that FAP-CAR EVs are capable of systemic circulation and payload delivery, showing a significant increase in accumulation within the liver and spleen compared to free Cy5.5. These findings suggest that CAR engineering enhances the ability of FAP-CAR EVs to inhibit TAF proliferation and induce apoptosis. FAP-targeting CAR EVs are positioned as a targeted bioengineered delivery platform with the potential for remodeling the tumor microenvironment and slowing the progression of desmoplasia in GBM.

title: A mitochondria-targeting dual-emissive probe for imaging hypoxia-associated biomarkers in early non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
authors: Zhou X, Gu R, Zou Y, Rajalakshmi K, Lee DK, Song JW, Nam YS, Zhu D
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Hypoxia, characterized by a deficiency of oxygen, is associated with the progression of various diseases and the formation of solid tumors. Prolonged hypoxia increases mitochondrial viscosity and induces mitochondrial autophagy, making these important biomarkers of hypoxic conditions. Herein, we developed MI-NO2, a dual-responsive fluorescent probe for the simultaneous detection of nitroreductase (NTR) activity and viscosity. Upon enzymatic reduction by NTR, MI-NO2 is converted to MI, resulting in enhanced intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) and a fluorescence turn-on response in the green channel. The sensing mechanism was confirmed by 1H NMR, HR-MS, HPLC, and DFT calculations. In addition, MI-NO2 exhibited enhanced fluorescence in the yellow channel under high-viscosity conditions owing to suppression of the twisted ICT (TICT) process. The probe successfully visualized mitochondrial hypoxia in living cells and distinguished hypoxic from normoxic conditions. Moreover, MI-NO2 enabled monitoring of hypoxia and the associated increase in viscosity increase in an early-stage mouse model of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. Importantly, the probe facilitated the sequential detection of hypoxia-related biomarkers, namely NTR activity and viscosity, using separate fluorescence channels without spectral cross-talk. MI-NO2 therefore provides an imaging platform for the early diagnosis of hypoxia-associated diseases.

title: Hepatic ITGBL1 promotes fibrogenesis and ductular remodeling through integrin-dependent latent TGF-β activation.
authors: He MK, Chen YH, Chen KC, Huang CT, Tang CC, Yang DJ, Lee CH, Hsu CC
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
abstract: Liver fibrosis is a major determinant of chronic liver disease progression and hepatobiliary remodeling. However, extracellular regulators linking fibrogenesis to pathological biliary responses remain incompletely understood. Integrin beta-like protein 1 (ITGBL1) is an extracellular matrix-associated protein implicated in integrin modulation, but its functional role in chronic liver injury remains unclear. A liver-specific doxycycline (DOX)-inducible zebrafish model was established to evaluate the effects of hepatic ITGBL1 gain-of-function in vivo. Fibrogenic and biliary responses were assessed using histologic, molecular, and genetic approaches. Mechanistic studies tested pathway dependence on itgav and ltbp1 using liver-specific genetic ablation, with cilengitide used as a complementary RGD-integrin pharmacologic perturbation. Hepatocyte-specific ITGBL1 induction triggered progressive hepatic stellate cell activation, extracellular matrix accumulation, and chronic fibrotic remodeling. Sustained ITGBL1 expression further promoted ductular reaction and biliary epithelial expansion during chronic liver injury progression. Genetic disruption of itgav or ltbp1 attenuated SMAD3 activation, collagen deposition, fibrogenic transcriptional programs, and associated histological remodeling; cilengitide independently attenuated fibrogenic readouts. These data support a working model in which hepatic ITGBL1 lies upstream of integrin/LTBP1-dependent latent TGF-β/SMAD3 signaling and provide a mechanistic framework for further resolving the molecular interactions among ITGBL1, ITGAV, and LTBP1 and the αv-integrin heterodimer involved. This pathway may represent a therapeutic target for fibrosis-associated biliary remodeling.

title: DUF6383-domain containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis predicts survival in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis.
authors: Kreimeyer H, Gonzalez C, Fondevila MF, AlcHepNet Investigators, Canbay A, Stärkel P, Gonzalez DJ, Schnabl B
abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis is a hallmark of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) characterized by a higher abundance of unfavorable species and a reduction of beneficial species. In this study, we aimed to analyze the bacterial proteome of stool samples from patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) (n = 80), alcohol use disorder (AUD; n = 20), and controls (n = 19) from an international multicenter cohort using quantitative tandem mass tag (TMT)-based metaproteomic profiling. We validated our results in an independent multicenter cohort of 72 patients with AH at the genomic level using qPCR. We detected 2,364 bacterial proteins and identified distinct metaproteomic signatures separating controls, patients with AUD, and AH. Patients with AUD and AH were characterized by depletion of Firmicutes-derived proteins and enrichment of proteins from Bacteroidetes, Proteobacteria, and Actinobacteria. Eighteen bacterial proteins increased with disease severity, many with multifunctional "moonlighting" roles, including enolase and hexokinase. DUF6383 domain-containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis is correlated with histological injury, inflammatory cell infiltration, and is linked to neutrophil degranulation in the host. Patients with a high abundance of DUF6383 domain-containing protein had significantly lower 90-day survival, and this association was validated by qPCR at the genomic level in a second cohort. Our findings show that microbial proteins are associated with disease severity and progression, and that DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P. distasonis is a potential prognostic biomarker for AH.

title: Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression and changes in the fibrosis-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD.
authors: Okuma H
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common in type 2 diabetes. We investigated the association between monocyte mRNA expression of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2), the molecular target of luseogliflozin, and changes in the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index during treatment with this agent. METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study used prospectively collected peripheral blood monocyte samples from 82 participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD who had received luseogliflozin for at least 6 months. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was measured using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Clinical and laboratory parameters, including FIB-4 index, were evaluated at baseline and 6 months after luseogliflozin initiation. Changes were calculated as the 6-month value minus the baseline value; therefore, negative values indicated reductions. RESULTS: After 6 months, waist circumference, hemoglobin A1c, liver enzyme levels, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and the FIB-4 index decreased significantly. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was negatively correlated with the change in the FIB-4 index, indicating that higher baseline expression was associated with a greater reduction. In multiple regression analyses, natural-log-transformed baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression remained associated with the change in the FIB-4 index after adjustment for baseline clinical variables. CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was associated with a greater reduction in the FIB-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment. This finding should be interpreted as an exploratory association between a cell-specific transcriptomic feature and changes in a fibrosis-related index, rather than as evidence of functional SGLT2 signaling in monocytes or histological fibrosis regression. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13340-026-00941-2.

Long-term trajectories of invasive hemodynamic parameters and clinical outcomes after durable left ventricular assist device implantation.
authors: Legtenberg S, Ter Maaten JM, Erasmus ME, Kuijpers M, Douglas YL, Droogh JM, de Felice E, van den Broek SAJ
abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term hemodynamic changes after durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation are not well characterized. Characterizing these trajectories is clinically relevant, as persistent or evolving abnormalities in filling pressures and pulmonary circulation may identify patients at risk for adverse outcomes. METHOD: We conducted a retrospective single-center study including all patients who underwent durable LVAD implantation at the University Medical Center Groningen (2012 to 2025). We evaluated serial right heart catheterization (RHC) measurements to describe hemodynamic trajectories. Repeated measures, mixed-effect models were used to analyze hemodynamic trajectories up to 60 months of follow-up, including mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP), pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP), right atrial pressure (RAP), and pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi). Trajectories were compared according to survivor status, baseline LVAD strategy, development of late right ventricular failure (RVF), presence of aortic regurgitation (AR), and worsening renal function (WRF). RESULTS: Among 199 patients (176 HeartMate 3; 23 HeartMate II), mean PAP (-10.1 mmHg, 95% CI -13.1 to -7.1) and PCWP (-9.9 mmHg, 95% CI -12.5 to -7.2) decreased significantly within the first 6 months after LVAD implantation, while RAP (0.0 mmHg, 95% CI -0.8 to 0.8) remained unchanged. Cardiac index (+0.6 L/min/m², 95% CI 0.4-0.8) and cardiac output (+1.3 L/min, 95% CI 0.9-1.7) increased significantly over the same interval. Beyond 6 months, trajectories for most hemodynamic parameters remained generally stable. Non-survivors and patients developing late RVF showed consistently higher filling pressures with trajectories largely parallel to those of survivors or those without RVF. Hemodynamic trajectories did not differ by initial LVAD strategy. In contrast, clinically significant aortic regurgitation and WRF were associated with distinct hemodynamic trajectories. CONCLUSION: Hemodynamic parameters after durable LVAD implantation improved early and remained largely stable thereafter. Patients with adverse clinical outcomes showed persistently higher and/or altered hemodynamic profiles. These findings suggest that longitudinal hemodynamic assessment may enable early identification of patients at risk for adverse outcomes.

title: Structure-constrained language-assisted diffusion model for unpaired low-dose computed tomography angiography reconstruction.
authors: Zhang G, Wang Z, Gao Z, Xu L, Zhou Z, Yu H, Zhang J, Liu X
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: The application of iodinated contrast media (ICM) improves the sensitivity and specificity of computed tomography (CT) for a wide range of clinical indications. However, high ICM doses can cause problems such as kidney damage and life-threatening allergic reactions. Deep learning methods can generate CT images of normal-dose ICM from low-dose ICM, reducing the required dose while maintaining diagnostic power. However, existing methods struggle to achieve accurate enhancement with incompletely paired images, mainly because of the limited ability of the model to recognize specific structures. To overcome this limitation, we propose a Structure-constrained Language-assisted Diffusion Model (SLDM), a unified medical generation model that integrates structural synergy and spatial intelligence. First, the structural prior information of the image is effectively extracted to constrain the model inference process, thus ensuring structural consistency in the enhancement process. Subsequently, a language-assisted strategy with spatial intelligence is introduced, which integrates the functions of visual perception and spatial reasoning, thus prompting the model to achieve accurate enhancement. Finally, the subtraction angiography enhancement module is applied, which serves to improve the contrast of the ICM region to suitable interval for observation. Qualitative analysis of visual comparison and quantitative results of several metrics demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in angiographic reconstruction for low-dose contrast medium CT angiography.

Integrated metabolic and process engineering of Rhodotorula toruloides for light-driven hydrocarbon production.
authors: Zhao H, Zhang Y, Lyu L, Lu H, Zhao ZK
abstract: Long-chain hydrocarbons are bulky chemicals traditionally produced via petroleum refining. Microbial production of these hydrocarbons from renewable resources has attracted much attention, but is limited by precursor accessibility and catalysis efficiency. Here, we combined genetic engineering and photobioprocess optimization for blue-light-driven hydrocarbon production by the oleaginous yeast Rhodotorula toruloides. Cytosolic expression of the Chlorella variabilis fatty acid photodecarboxylase (CvFAP) in R. toruloides conferred cells producing 15.0 mg/L hydrocarbons, while targeting CvFAP to lipid droplets (LDs) via fusion with the LD-associated protein Ldp1 enhanced titer by more than 3-fold. Systematic optimization of blue-light fermentation further doubled hydrocarbon titers. Metabolic rewiring of the pathways related to fatty acid activation, lipid turnover, and carotenoid biosynthesis showed that CRT1 deletion had the most pronounced effect, increasing hydrocarbon titer by 2.5-fold. Additional improvements were achieved by reinforcing free fatty acid supply and increasing CvFAP copy number. The final strain R. toruloides NF72D produced 557.7 mg/L hydrocarbons in flask culture, over 37-fold higher than that by the initial cytosolic expression strain. Collectively, this study demonstrates the importance of proper localization of key enzymes for improved biosynthesis of fatty acid-derived metabolites and a great potential for light-driven production of renewable hydrocarbons by oleaginous yeasts.

title: Systematic metabolic engineering for trans-aconitic acid production in Aspergillus niger.
authors: Wang S, He J, Li W, Cui C, Liu J, Liu H
abstract: Trans-aconitate (TAA) is a valuable bio-based chemical for nematicides and polymer synthesis. We repurposed the industrial citrate producer Aspergillus niger for efficient TAA biosynthesis. Heterologous AexA enabled extracellular aconitate export. However, overexpressing aconitases from various sources, targeted to the cytoplasm or mitochondria, failed to increase titers. Although mitochondria proved the optimal site for cis-aconitate accumulation, the bottleneck likely persisted due to thermodynamic constraints. To overcome this, we designed a push-pull strategy: a pull module using mitochondrial MttA to export cis-aconitate to the cytosol, where TbrA isomerizes it to TAA, coupled with a push module enhancing cytosolic acetyl-CoA via the phosphoketolase pathway. Multicopy tbrA expression was critical. The final strain produced 34.30 g/L total aconitate (>90% TAA) in a 5-L bioreactor within 6 days. This work highlights a compartmentalized push-pull strategy exploiting mitochondrial-cytosolic organization to convert a citrate chassis into a high-yield TAA cell factory.

title: Disrupting the cholesterol-mechanics axis enables ferroptosis and deep drug delivery in hepatocellular carcinoma.
authors: Zhu J, Zhong Y, Yan S, Zeng X
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops within a fibrotic and stiffened microenvironment that limits drug penetration and suppresses regulated cell death, contributing to therapeutic resistance. Here we identify cholesterol as a central regulator linking extracellular matrix (ECM) mechanics to ferroptosis resistance through lipid raft‒mediated mechanotransduction. Spatial transcriptomics of human HCC specimens reveals enrichment of PTK2 (focal adhesion kinase, FAK) and cholesterol-associated pathways at tumor-stroma interfaces, implicating a cholesterol-mechanics axis in tumor progression. To target this vulnerability, we engineer a one-dimensional Fe-Mn oxyhydroxide nanozyme integrated with cholesterol oxidase (FeMnOOH/C). This platform simultaneously depletes cholesterol, disrupts lipid raft signaling, and remodels ECM stiffness, while amplifying ferroptosis through multienzymatic redox catalysis. FeMnOOH/C enhances membrane fluidity, promotes deep tumor penetration, and enables efficient intratumoral delivery of therapeutics. In vivo, FeMnOOH/C induces robust ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death, leading to increased cytotoxic T cell infiltration and marked tumor suppression. These findings establish mechano-metabolic reprogramming (mechanical regulation and cholesterol deprivation) as a strategy to overcome ferroptosis resistance and provide proof-of-concept support for a strategy of targeting fibrotic tumors.

title: A benchmarking framework for organoid computing.
authors: Xing Y, Gao Y, Hong Z, Tian C, Cai H, Chu H, Yang Y, Liang PY
abstract: Organoid computing leverages functional neural networks of lab-grown neural organoids to recapitulate key aspects of human brain information processing, holding promising potential in brain-inspired computing, brain-computer interfaces, neuroscience, and medicine. However, its broad application remains constrained due to technical limitations including biological variability, interface instability, stochastic performance, and limited reproducibility. Here, we present a benchmarking framework that systematically quantifies the key performance determinants of organoid computing. We operationally define 'benchmark-ready' organoid substrates using optional criteria encompassing viability, cellular identity, structural integrity, functional maturation, and baseline networks, supported by multimodal phenotyping. We further establish qualification metrics for organoid-machine interface and intrinsic neural and network function, including physical coupling, spatial coverage, temporal stability, spontaneous activity, and network-level organization. Finally, we introduce a hierarchical evaluation framework for stimulation-evoked computation combined with information encoding criteria, standardized scoring, and statistical reporting. We believe that the benchmarking framework may provide an adaptable foundation for standardized, reproducible and comparable evaluation of organoid computing technologies, thereby facilitating the broad adoption and application of organoid intelligence.

title: 3D culture-derived MSC EV facilitate repair by activating microglial autophagy in spinal cord injury.
authors: Liu H, Li X, Li M, Jiu J, Zhao Y, Li D, Zhang J, Yan L
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is characterized by persistent neuroinflammation, neuronal loss, and limited tissue repair. Extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stromal cells (hUC-MSC-EVs) represent a promising cell-free therapeutic approach, although strategies for improving their bioactivity and regulating their cargo composition remain incompletely defined. Here, a gelatin microcarrier-based three-dimensional (3D) culture system was used to generate hUC-MSC-EVs. Compared with EVs generated under conventional two-dimensional (2D) culture conditions, 3D EVs reduced lesion severity, improved functional recovery, and promoted reparative-like changes in ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule 1(Iba1)-positive microglia/macrophages in a rat SCI model. Transcriptomic, tandem-reporter, and pharmacological analyses indicated that intact autophagic processing contributes to the reparative-like phenotypic effects of 3D EVs in microglial cells. Comparative microRNA (miRNA) profiling identified miRNA-99a-5p as one of the enriched candidates, and gain- and loss-of-function experiments supported its contribution to autophagy-related and phenotype-associated responses in recipient microglia. The 3D culture condition was accompanied by increased nuclear localization of Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), increased expression of Y-box binding protein 1 (YBX1), TEA domain transcription factor 4 (TEAD4) occupancy at selected YBX1 promoter regions, and higher EV-associated miR-99a-5p abundance. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) analysis further demonstrated an association between YBX1 and miR-99a-5p. Overall, these findings indicate that 3D culture is associated with EV cargo remodeling and improved therapeutic effects after SCI, while miR-99a-5p represents one functional EV-associated cargo contributing to selected microglial responses.

title: Dynamic UV-Vis monitoring of ternary pharmaceutical photodegradation using multivariate curve resolution and predictive modeling.
authors: Ocampo DEM, Martínez SS
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) photodegradation of multicomponent pharmaceutical systems generates complex spectral signals due to overlapping absorption bands and transient intermediates, limiting conventional quantitative approaches. To address this challenge, an integrated chemometric strategy was developed to predict concentration profiles in dynamic ternary mixtures of paracetamol (PAR), naproxen sodium (NPX), and diclofenac sodium (DIC) in spiked river water using Ultraviolet-visible (UV-Vis) spectroscopy. UV-Vis spectra from individual photolysis experiments were analyzed by Multivariate Curve Resolution-Alternating Least Squares (MCR-ALS) to estimate concentration profiles of the parent pharmaceuticals. These profiles were associated with ternary mixture spectra reconstructed by linear combination of the spectral data obtained from the individual photolysis experiments. The combined spectral data, together with experimentally acquired calibration data, served as input to develop a linear Partial Least Squares (PLS) and non-linear Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models, enabling simultaneous prediction of component concentrations. The degree of nonlinearity in the calibration datasets was first assessed using the Non-Linearity Degree (NLD), yielding values of 0.248, 0.398, and 0.214 for PAR, NPX, and DIC, respectively. These results exceeded the 0.05 threshold, indicating significant non-linear behavior in the calibration datasets. Accordingly, the linear PLS model showed limited predictive performance, particularly for DIC. In contrast, the non-linear ANN model achieved higher predictive accuracy, demonstrating its superior suitability for the dynamically evolving multicomponent systems.

title: DA-S2RL: Disease-aware shared-specific representation learning for heterogeneous image-EHR Alzheimer's disease diagnosis.
authors: Wang W, Shi Y, Cheng J, Liu Y
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: Combining electronic health records (EHR) with medical images is important for improving the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, neuroimages and EHR differ greatly in semantic content and data distribution. Neuroimages mainly reflect brain structure and metabolic abnormalities, while EHR records clinical symptoms and behavioral changes. Directly fusing these heterogeneous modalities may mix shared disease information with modality-specific diagnostic cues, resulting in redundant and ambiguous representations. To address this problem, we propose DA-S2RL, a disease-aware shared-specific multimodal representation learning framework for AD diagnosis. DA-S2RL organizes heterogeneous image and EHR features into disease-related shared semantics and modality-specific diagnostic residuals. The core of DA-S2RL is the shared-specific cross-modal coding (SCC) module. It strengthens cross-modal semantic consistency, suppresses redundant correlations, and enables mutual refinement between shared semantics and diagnostic residuals. Before SCC, image features are integrated into a compact image representation, and EHR features are encoded into the same feature space. Experiments on ADNI and NACC demonstrate that explicitly organizing heterogeneous image-EHR representations into shared disease semantics and modality-specific residuals improves multimodal diagnostic learning under different image-EHR settings.

title: PSMA-targeted nanoparticles delivering ATR and Src/Bcr-Abl inhibitors to stimulate STING and reprogram senescence-associated secretory phenotype for enhancing immunotherapy in prostate cancer.
authors: Wang W, Liu H, Liu Y, Wang H, Wen X, Tian Z, Yin H, Yang T
abstract: Significant increases in the proportion of senescent cells were observed in prostate cancer following endocrine therapy. Although treatment-induced senescence (TIS) effectively suppresses cancer cell proliferation, the long-term accumulation of the immunosuppressive senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) promotes immune evasion, leading to the failure of immunotherapy. Herein, a liposomal nanoparticle (T-Lipo@Das/Ber) encapsulating the ATR inhibitor Berzosertib and the Src/Bcr-Abl inhibitor Dasatinib was designed, which can target prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA). T-Lipo@Das/Ber efficiently enters cells via PSMA-mediated endocytosis. On the one hand, Berzosertib inhibits ATR, increases DNA damage, and induces the release of type I interferons and pro-inflammatory factors via the cGAS-STING pathway, ultimately enhancing tumor immunogenicity. On the other hand, by inhibiting the Src/Bcr-Abl pathway, Dasatinib reprograms the SASP, reducing the secretion of immunosuppressive factors while promoting the exposure of calreticulin (CRT) and the release of high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), thereby synergistically recruiting and activating immune cells. With the stimulation of both innate and adaptive immune responses, "immune cold tumor" is transformed into "immune hot tumor". When combined with αPD-1, it not only effectively inhibits the growth of the primary tumor, but also induces long-term immune memory to prevent tumor recurrence.

title: A fluorinated poly(amino acid) nanovaccine with spatiotemporally encoded innate priming and antigen cross-presentation for tumor immunotherapy.
authors: Wang Z, Su Y, Zhang S, Yu B, Wei Y, Liu H, Veselova IA, Lv S
abstract: The efficacy of cancer vaccines depends on spatiotemporally coordinated innate immune priming and antigen cross-presentation, but this hierarchy remains difficult to control with existing delivery platforms. Here, we report a fluorinated diethylenetriamine-modified poly(aspartic acid) nanovaccine platform, termed DET-F, and identify DET-F30 as the optimized formulation for antigen delivery and immune activation. Perfluorooctyl side chains promote early endosomal toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) associated innate immune signaling and dendritic cell maturation, whereas the pH-responsive polymer backbone facilitates subsequent endosomal escape and cytosolic antigen release. This chemically encoded sequence enables delayed yet enhanced antigen cross-presentation in mature dendritic cells. DET-F30/antigen nanoparticles display efficient antigen loading and cellular uptake, activate TLR3-related innate immune pathways, and elicit robust antigen-specific CD8+ T cell immunity. In multiple tumor models, DET-F30-based vaccination suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, prolongs survival, and enhances post-surgical anti-PD-1 therapy. This work establishes fluorinated poly(amino acid)s as minimalist self-adjuvant nanovaccine vectors and demonstrates that precise polymer-architecture encoding can orchestrate sequential innate immune activation and antigen processing for improved cancer immunotherapy.
